Definition: Integration of driver's license registration and traffic offence data
Comments: Chad announced plan for integrated digital platform for transport services (September 2025), to centralize driver licenses, vehicle registration, technical inspection, transport licenses into single platform. Still in planning stage, not yet operational.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed and corroborated with three further sources. The September 2025 transport-ministry announcement to centralise driver's licences, vehicle registration and transport permits was still at planning stage as of February 2026, when talks with Azerbaijan on 'smart transport systems' remained at the discussion stage and a related but distinct waybill/axle-tax (LVO) dematerialisation pilot launched separately for freight, not driver licensing. No evidence driver-licence data is yet integrated into any exchange, so Planned (2) stands.

Definition: Integration of social assistance programs, grant registries, beneficiary management systems
Comments: Mobile money used for some cash transfer payments to community teachers and in some areas outside main cities. However, no integrated social protection registry or G2P digital payment system documented.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Upgraded from Planned to Under development. World Bank SASPP documentation (updated September 2025) confirms Chad's Unified Social Registry (RSU) is operational with 684,500 households registered, mobile digital payments have been used for cash transfers since 2022 (COVID-19 and refugee responses), and the RSU is being actively linked to ANATS's biometric ID registry for beneficiary/refugee verification. This is more than a paper plan, but full interoperability with a national data exchange remains a stated 2025-2030 goal rather than an achieved integration, so 'Partially integrated' (4) is not yet supported.

Definition: Whether primary laws, acts, or legal instruments exist that establish authority for cross-government data sharing and govern the data exchange system
Comments: Package of 5 laws adopted in 2015: consumer protection (No. 005/PR/2015), ANSICE establishment (No. 006/PR/2015), personal data protection (No. 007/PR/2015), electronic transactions (No. 008/PR/2015), cybersecurity (No. 009/PR/2015). October 2025: National Assembly approved ordinance amending 2014 electronic communications law. New comprehensive digital law finalizing in December 2025. However, World Bank notes legislation is not yet fully applied in practice.
redteam_note: Comment wording may not match the score — re-read (needs judgement).
revision_notes: Revised down from Yes to Under development. The 2015 package (confirmed via ARCEP's official legal register: Laws 005-009/PR/2015) covers data protection, cybersecurity, e-transactions, consumer protection and creates ANSICE, but none of these specifically establishes authority for cross-government data sharing or governs a data exchange system as such. The World Bank's Chad Digital Economy Diagnostic explicitly states no shared data-governance/interoperability legal framework yet exists, and as of May 2026 Chad is actively drafting a new 'Code du Numérique' and national data-governance strategy to fill precisely this gap — confirming the specific enabling legislation for data exchange remains under development, not yet in force. Flagged review resolved in favour of a lower score given the mismatch between the definition (cross-government data sharing authority) and the cited laws (data protection/cybersecurity generally).
